author: BrentDesk Staff
headline: Formulators buy a year's chemistry in three days at the Dubai coatings show
deck: The Middle East Coatings Show functions as an annual procurement round for regional paint and coatings manufacturers.
excerpt: The Middle East Coatings Show serves regional coatings formulators as a concentrated annual procurement round, with a published exhibitor directory carrying stand allocations.
content:
The Middle East Coatings Show opens at Expo City in Dubai on 28 September, and for the regional coatings industry it functions as something closer to an annual procurement round than a general trade exhibition.

The organiser has published a live exhibitor directory with stand allocations. Confirmed raw material and additive suppliers include ADDAPT Chemicals at NB31, Admark Polycoats at NB11, Akripol Kimya at NH89, Alliance Organics at ND79, Anhui Feiyan Pigment at NI131, Anadolu Mikronize at ND109 and 3M EMEA at NG101. BYK holds the gold sponsorship, with Tronox, Wacker Chemicals Middle East, Netzsch and Safic-Alcan Necarbo also exhibiting.

That directory matters commercially because of how coatings formulators buy. A paint manufacturer's product range depends on a portfolio of binders, pigments, additives and solvents sourced from many suppliers, and the technical relationship with each is ongoing rather than transactional. A formulator walking this floor is meeting existing suppliers about next year's supply, evaluating substitutes for materials that have become expensive or constrained, and assessing new chemistry against formulations already in production.

Concentrating that into three days has real efficiency. The alternative is a year of individual supplier visits, and for a mid-sized regional formulator with a small technical team, the exhibition is the more practical route to the same coverage.

The published stand allocations support that use directly. A visitor with a defined sourcing list can plan a route through the halls, which is a different mode of attendance from browsing, and it is why the directory is more than a courtesy.

The exhibitor profile — weighted toward raw materials rather than finished paint brands — confirms the audience. This is a business-to-business event for manufacturers, not a showcase for specifiers or contractors, and the products on show are inputs rather than outputs.

The Gulf's position in that value chain is worth restating. Regional petrochemical capacity supplies binder and solvent volume competitively, while the specialty additives that determine a coating's performance in this climate remain largely imported from a concentrated international supplier base. The show is where that gap is negotiated each year.

The organiser gives more than 350 exhibiting brands from over 24 countries across roughly 15,000 square metres, with more than 5,000 visitors expected. ChemTalks is the accompanying knowledge programme. Those figures are the organiser's own, and exhibitor and stand detail is taken from its published directory.

ChemTalks runs alongside as the knowledge programme, with session detail published through the organiser's agenda platform.

Protective and industrial coatings form the segment with most direct relevance to Gulf industrial operators, where coating specification determines the corrosion maintenance interval on plant for decades after construction.
